items.q: A PdfWriter is told writer.append('a.pdf', (0, 5, 2)). Which page indexes are copied?
rationales: A tuple of three integers is read like range(0, 5, 2), so every second page is taken, not every page.
A tuple is a range, not a list of the pages to copy; 5 is the stop value and is never copied.

items.q: Writing writer.append('a.pdf', [0, 5]) for a six-page file copies which pages?
options: Page index 0 and page index 5 only
Nothing, because a list is not accepted
rationales: That is what the tuple (0, 5) does; a list names the pages one by one.
append() accepts a list, and in the library run it copied two pages.

items.q: In Project 12 the call is writer.append(name, (1, len(reader.pages))). What does it add for a PDF of one page?
rationales: The range starts at index 1, so the first page is always left out and a one-page file gives an empty range.
An empty range is not an error; the library run combined a one-page file with two others without one.

items.q: Project 12, with its name error corrected, is run twice in the same folder. Why does the second combined.pdf have more pages?
options: append() remembers the pages of the earlier run
combined.pdf is itself a .pdf file in the folder and is read as an input
rationales: The writer is a new object on every run and keeps nothing.
os.listdir() returns each name once; the extra pages come from the output file being listed.

options: Places the other page on top of the existing content
Replaces the page's content with the other page
Places the other page underneath the page's existing content
rationales: Putting it on top is over=True, which the pypdf documentation calls a stamp or overlay.
The contents are combined, not replaced.

items.q: After reader.decrypt('an incorrect password'), what is the name of the value it returns?
rationales: That name is returned when the owner password was the one given.
The error is raised when pages are read before a successful decrypt, not by decrypt() itself.

items.q: A paragraph holds plain text, then a bold word, then plain text, then an italic word. How many Run objects does it have?
rationales: A run ends whenever the style changes, and there are four stretches of text.
A paragraph with one run would have a single style throughout.

items.q: A run's bold attribute is None. What decides whether its text is shown in bold?
options: Nothing; the text is never bold
rationales: False, not None, switches bold off for good.
The text of a paragraph carries no styling; styling is held by runs and styles.

items.q: Which name applies the linked style whose paragraph form is 'Quote' to a Run?
rationales: The paragraph name was refused for a run with ValueError in the library run.
Python-Docx looks up a style by its name; 'Quote Run' is not one, and the linked style uses ' Char'.

items.q: pypdf 6.19.0 encrypts a PDF with writer.encrypt('pw') and no algorithm. What did the library run show?
options: The older RC4 encryption, version 2 revision 3
No encryption, because an algorithm is required
rationales: That is what algorithm='AES-256' wrote; the default is RC4, which the documentation calls insecure.
The call succeeded and wrote an encrypted file.

items.q: What does doc.add_heading('Top', 0) add to a Python-Docx document?
options: A paragraph in a style called Heading 0
Nothing; it raises ValueError for level 0
A paragraph in the Title style
rationales: Level 0 gives Title, and Heading 1 is the first numbered heading.
Levels 0 to 9 are accepted; the error came at level 10.
